card.name: Linking words before drug effect verbs
card.fires_on: Small linking words (to, that, which, has, will not, might) in drug-interaction sentences. They sit right before a verb saying what a drug does, such as decrease, cause, depress or be additive.

modes.label: to before effect verb
modes.description: The word 'to' after 'expected', 'likely' or 'sufficient', just before a verb of drug effect.
modes.example: Benzodiazepines and opioids would be expected<< to>> decrease the MAC of sevofl

modes.label: relative word after a drug
modes.description: 'that' or 'which' after a drug or drug class, introducing what it does.
modes.example: Other drugs<< that>> cause CNS depression (e.g., sed

modes.label: auxiliary verb
modes.description: Helper verbs such as has, will not or might before a past participle or predicate about a drug.
modes.example: and only after the alpha blocker<< has>> been initiated.

card.writes: It seems to push the next word toward verbs like render or affect and away from give or giving.
card.plain: It marks the small word in an interaction sentence just before the text says what one drug does to the body or to another drug.
